binders: In the first conjunct: for every natural number n, every real p bundled with 0 ≤ p ≤ 1, and every vertex v in Fin n.
In the second conjunct: there exists a single real constant c, and within its scope, for every natural number n, every real p bundled with 0 ≤ p ≤ 1, and every vertex v in Fin n.
hypotheses: The parameter p is restricted by its subtype to the closed interval [0,1].
The existential witness c must satisfy 0 < c.
There are no other explicit hypotheses; in particular, the exact-law conjunct is asserted rather than assumed when stating the tail-bound conjunct.
conclusions: For every n,p,v, the natural-valued random variable G ↦ degree_G(v), under the graph measure obtained from the Bernoulli edge-set measure on non-loop unordered pairs, has exactly the Binomial(n - 1,p) measure on Nat as its law.

There exists one real c > 0 such that, simultaneously for every n,p,v, the real-valued mass under the same graph measure of the event {|degree_G(v) - ((n:Real)-1)p| ≥ (1/10)((n:Real)-1)p} is at most 2 exp(-c((n:Real)-1)p).
mathematical_definitions: Let μ_{n,p} denote the first field of LocalDef003 n p. It is the measure on simple graphs obtained by pulling the set-Bernoulli measure on non-diagonal unordered pairs of vertices back along the edge-set representation.
Let X_{n,p,v}(G) denote the second field of LocalDef003 n p evaluated at v and G. It is degree_G(v), the natural-number cardinality of {w | G.Adj v w}.
Let β_{n,p} denote LocalDef004 n p, the Nat-valued Binomial(n - 1,p) measure. Its PMF has masses choose(n-1,i) p^i (1-p)^((n-1)-i) on i from 0 through n - 1, with natural subtraction used in n - 1.
Let m_{n,p} = ((n:Real)-1)p. The deviation event is A_{n,p,v} = {G | |(X_{n,p,v}(G):Real) - m_{n,p}| ≥ m_{n,p}/10}.
The event mass in the second conjunct is (μ_{n,p}(A_{n,p,v})).toReal.
translation.proposition_plain_english: The proposition is the conjunction of two assertions. First, for every graph size n, probability parameter p in [0,1], and vertex v of Fin n, the number of neighbors of v in a graph sampled from the Bernoulli edge-set measure on simple graphs has the Binomial(n - 1,p) law. Second, there is one absolute real constant c > 0, independent of n, p, and v, such that the probability mass of a degree deviation of at least ten percent of ((n:Real)-1)p from that center is bounded by 2 times exp(-c((n:Real)-1)p).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The parameter p is restricted to the closed interval [0,1].

The quantification over v : Fin n makes both universal assertions vacuous at n = 0. Whenever a vertex v is actually present, n ≥ 1, so the real expression (n:Real)-1 is nonnegative and agrees with the cast of the natural predecessor n - 1.

At p = 0, and also at n = 1 when a vertex exists, the center and threshold are zero; the displayed event uses ≥ and is therefore the whole sample space if the degree is zero, while the right side equals 2, so the tail inequality is non-informative. More generally, parameter regimes in which 2 exp(-c((n:Real)-1)p) ≥ 1 give a probability bound that may be trivial.
Only the fixed relative threshold 1/10 is asserted; there is no general deviation parameter or family of Chernoff bounds in the proposition.
The single witness c is outside the n,p,v quantifiers, so it must be uniform in all three variables and cannot depend on them.
The event includes equality because it is defined by threshold ≤ absolute deviation.

The first exact-law assertion and the second tail assertion are separate conjuncts. The tail assertion does not logically take the exact-law assertion as a premise, even though both refer to the same packaged graph law and degree statistic.

Measure.real applies ENNReal.toReal. The proposition itself does not separately state finiteness or a probability-measure typeclass assumption for μ_{n,p}; any such guarantee must come from the fixed definition of the graph measure.

The graph distribution is encoded by a pullback of ProbabilityTheory.setBernoulli on non-diagonal unordered vertex pairs rather than by explicit quantified edge-independence statements in the target itself.
ambiguities: SimpleGraph.binomialRandom is expanded only as a pullback of ProbabilityTheory.setBernoulli along edgeSet; the packet does not expand setBernoulli, edgeSet, Sym2.diagSet, or set complement. Thus the usual independent-edge interpretation is strongly indicated but not fully reconstructible from the supplied bodies alone.

The packet gives only the type, not constructors or fields, of ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw. It can be translated conventionally as exact equality of the pushforward law (with associated measurability conditions), but its exact internal proposition is not recoverable from the supplied material.

LocalDef005 is only described by its type, constructor signature, and two projections; this suffices to identify the two packaged components used here, but not any additional definitional or recursor behavior of the inductive type.
